cls: Cardiovascular - neprilysin inhibitor (used as sacubitril/valsartan, Entresto)
pharm: Neprilysin inhibitor combined with the ARB valsartan; raises natriuretic peptides (vasodilation, natriuresis) while blocking angiotensin II
tags: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
quick: Sacubitril/valsartan 49/51 mg BID, double every 2-4 weeks to target 97/103 mg BID
Boxed fetal toxicity - stop immediately if pregnancy detected; contraindicated in pregnancy
No human milk data; avoid breastfeeding (fetal/neonatal concern with RAAS blockade)
No adjustment in mild-moderate impairment; monitor creatinine/K+; caution in severe
No adjustment in mild impairment; reduce starting dose in moderate; avoid in severe
Blood pressure, creatinine/eGFR, potassium, angioedema symptoms
summary: Sacubitril (available only as sacubitril/valsartan, Entresto) is a neprilysin-inhibitor/ARB combination for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (PARADIGM-HF mortality benefit over enalapril) and for hypertension. Neprilysin inhibition raises beneficial natriuretic peptides while valsartan blocks angiotensin. Boxed warning covers fetal toxicity. Concomitant ACE inhibitor use is contraindicated (angioedema risk) with a 36-hour washout in both directions; history of angioedema is also a contraindication.
indications: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (NYHA class II-IV) to reduce cardiovascular death and hospitalisation

dosage.d: Start 49/51 mg twice daily (or 24/26 mg BID if ACE/ARB-naive, severe renal impairment or moderate hepatic impairment); double every 2-4 weeks as tolerated to target 97/103 mg BID
dosage.t: With or without food at the same times daily
dosage.n: 36-hour ACE-inhibitor washout required before starting; never co-administer with an ACE inhibitor

dosage.d: Per regional labeling titration from low dose

admin: Take twice daily at the same times, with or without food
Stop any ACE inhibitor at least 36 hours before the first dose - never take both together
Stand up slowly (blood-pressure lowering); report swelling of face/lips/tongue immediately
Do not use potassium supplements or salt substitutes without asking (potassium rises)
moa: Sacubitril inhibits neprilysin, the enzyme degrading natriuretic peptides, bradykinin and adrenomedullin - raising vasodilatory/natriuretic signalling. Valsartan simultaneously blocks the angiotensin II type-1 receptor, preventing reflex RAAS activation. The combination reduces cardiac remodelling, preload and afterload in HFrEF.

absolute: Concomitant ACE inhibitor use (angioedema risk; 36-hour washout mandatory)
History of angioedema related to ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy
Concomitant aliskiren in diabetes (dual RAAS blockade)
relative: Severe renal impairment or bilateral renal-artery stenosis (creatinine/K+ rise)
History of angioedema of any cause (extreme caution)

preg: Drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause fetal injury and death when used in pregnancy. Discontinue sacubitril/valsartan immediately if pregnancy is detected. Advise effective contraception. Oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia, renal failure and death have been reported.
lact: No human milk data for sacubitril; valsartan appears in rat milk. Because of potential adverse effects in the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No starting-dose change in mild-moderate renal impairment; monitor creatinine and potassium after initiation and each uptitration. Use a lower starting dose (24/26 mg BID) in severe impairment; limited data in ESRD/dialysis.
hepatic: No adjustment in mild hepatic impairment. Reduce the starting dose (24/26 mg BID) in moderate impairment; avoid in severe impairment (Child-Pugh C).

major: ACE inhibitors (contraindicated - angioedema; 36-hour washout both ways)
Aliskiren in diabetes or renal impairment (dual RAAS blockade - avoid)
moderate: NSAIDs (blunt effect; renal injury and hyperkalaemia risk)
Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors and other vasodilators (additive hypotension)
interactions.food: With or without food; avoid potassium-containing salt substitutes unless approved.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may worsen dizziness and low blood pressure; avoid excess.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

emergency: Swelling of face, lips, tongue or throat, or breathing difficulty (angioedema) - stop drug and seek emergency care
Fainting or very low blood pressure with confusion - seek emergency care

monitoring: Serum creatinine/eGFR and potassium within 1-2 weeks of starting and each dose change
Heart-failure symptoms, weight and renal function long-term
counsel: Never take with an ACE inhibitor (ramipril, enalapril, lisinopril) - leave at least 36 hours between them
Swelling of face/lips/tongue or trouble breathing is an emergency - stop the drug and get help
Rise slowly; dizziness is common after dose increases
Avoid salt substitutes and potassium supplements unless approved; attend kidney and potassium blood tests
Stop and call immediately if you become pregnant
pk: Blood-pressure lowering within hours; HF benefit accrues over weeks-months
Sacubitril active metabolite ~2 hours; valsartan ~1.5-2 hours
Active sacubitril metabolite ~11-12 hours; valsartan ~9-10 hours (twice-daily dosing)
Room temperature 20-25 C; protect from moisture in original container
pearls: PARADIGM-HF stopped early for mortality benefit over enalapril - the basis for replacing ACE inhibitors in HFrEF
The 36-hour ACE washout in both directions is the critical safety step (angioedema mechanism via bradykinin)
Hypotension after switching usually reflects needed diuretic reduction, not automatic drug failure
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; never double up. Resume twice-daily dosing.
overdose: Overdose produces marked hypotension. Provide supportive care with supine positioning, IV fluids and vasopressors as needed; monitor renal function and potassium. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
